title: Bridge Truss Stress Analysis Viewer
prompt:
Create a single HTML file using Three.js that implements an interactive bridge truss stress analysis viewer with dynamic difficulty levels.

## Scene Setup
- Use a dark background (0x1a1a2e) with a perspective camera at position (0, 5, 20), looking at origin.
- Add ambient light (0x404060, intensity 0.4) and two directional lights: one from (10,15,10) white intensity 0.8, one from (-5,10,-5) blue-tinted (0x8888ff) intensity 0.3.
- Render a ground plane (50x50, color 0x2a2a3a) at y=0 with grid helper (50 divisions, 0x444466).
- Add OrbitControls for camera manipulation.

## Bridge Truss Structure
- Build a parametric Warren truss bridge along the X-axis, centered at origin.
- The bridge has configurable parameters: span length (default 16 units), height (default 3 units), number of panels (default 6).
- Nodes are rendered as small spheres (radius 0.15, metallic material). Members (beams) are rendered as cylinders connecting nodes.
- Bottom chord nodes sit at y=1. Top chord nodes sit at y=1+height. Diagonal members connect alternating top/bottom nodes in a zigzag pattern.
- Each member stores: startNodeIndex, endNodeIndex, length, crossSectionArea (default 0.05 m²), elasticModulus (default 200e9 Pa for steel).
- Color-code members by stress: blue (0x0066ff) for compression, red (0xff3300) for tension, green (0x00cc44) for near-zero stress (abs < 5% of max). Intensity scales with stress magnitude.

## Stress Analysis Engine
- Implement a simplified 2D truss analysis using the direct stiffness method (matrix method).
- Support nodes: pin support at bottom-left node (fixed x,y), roller support at bottom-right node (fixed y only).
- Apply a single point load at a user-selected node. Default load: -50 kN in Y direction at the midspan bottom chord node.
- Compute member axial forces, stresses (force/area), and node displacements.
- Visualize deformed shape by scaling displacements by a magnification factor (default 500x) and offsetting node positions.
- Show displacement vectors at each node as small arrows (ArrowHelper) scaled proportionally.

## Dynamic Difficulty System
- Three difficulty levels: 'basic', 'intermediate', 'advanced'.
- Basic: uniform cross-sections, single point load, steel only.
- Intermediate: user can modify individual member cross-section areas (click member, use +/- keys to adjust area by ±0.005 m²), two simultaneous loads allowed.
- Advanced: mixed materials (steel 200e9, aluminum 69e9, timber 12e9 Pa), thermal loading (+/- 30°C with alpha=12e-6 for steel), buckling check for compression members (Euler critical load = pi²*E*I/L² where I = area²/12 approximation). Members that exceed buckling load flash red with a warning icon.

## User Interactions
- Click on a node (raycasting) to select it as the load application point. Selected node glows yellow.
- Press 'L' to cycle load magnitude: -50kN, -100kN, -150kN, -200kN, then back to -50kN.
- Press 'D' to cycle difficulty: basic → intermediate → advanced → basic.
- Press 'M' to toggle deformed/undeformed shape display.
- Press 'T' to toggle thermal load on/off (only effective in advanced mode).
- Press 'U' to undo the last action (supports up to 10 undo steps). Press 'R' to redo.
- In intermediate/advanced mode, click a member to select it (highlighted with emissive glow), then press '+' or '-' to adjust its cross-section area.
- Press 'B' to toggle buckling check overlay (advanced mode only).
- Press 'Space' to reset everything to defaults.

## HUD / DOM UI
- Top-left panel showing: current difficulty, load magnitude, number of nodes, number of members, max tensile stress, max compressive stress, max displacement magnitude.
- Bottom bar showing: selected node index (or 'None'), selected member index (or 'None'), current member area if selected, material if in advanced mode.
- A color legend bar on the right side mapping blue→green→red for compression→zero→tension.
- All text uses monospace font, semi-transparent dark background panels.

## State Management (window.__3D_STATE__)
Expose the following on window.__3D_STATE__:
- difficulty: string ('basic'|'intermediate'|'advanced')
- loadMagnitude: number (in kN, e.g. -50)
- selectedNodeIndex: number|null
- selectedMemberIndex: number|null
- showDeformed: boolean
- thermalEnabled: boolean
- bucklingOverlay: boolean
- nodeCount: number
- memberCount: number
- memberForces: array of numbers (axial force per member in kN)
- memberStresses: array of numbers (stress per member in Pa)
- nodeDisplacements: array of {x, y} objects (displacement per node in meters)
- maxTensileStress: number (Pa)
- maxCompressiveStress: number (Pa, stored as negative)
- maxDisplacement: number (magnitude, meters)
- totalStrainEnergy: number (sum of 0.5 * force² * length / (E * A) for all members, in Joules)
- memberAreas: array of numbers (cross-section area per member)
- memberMaterials: array of strings ('steel'|'aluminum'|'timber') per member
- bucklingFlags: array of booleans (true if member exceeds Euler critical load)
- undoStackSize: number
- redoStackSize: number
- panelCount: number (number of truss panels)
- deformationScale: number (magnification factor)
- analysisValid: boolean (true if last analysis completed without NaN)

Ensure all numerical results are NaN-free. Recompute analysis on every parameter change. The analysis must satisfy equilibrium: sum of all external forces + reactions ≈ 0 (within 1e-6 tolerance).
physics_constraints: Static equilibrium: sum of reaction forces must equal applied loads (tolerance 1e-6). Strain energy must be non-negative. Stress = Force/Area. Euler buckling: Pcr = pi²EI/L². Thermal strain = alpha * deltaT. Displacements must be finite and bounded. Conservation: total external work ≈ total strain energy for linear elastic analysis.
